rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nouns with a radical final yāʾ or wāw preceded by kasra or ḍamma lose that weak letter in inflection and retain a preceding kasra.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن كل شيء كانت لامه ياء أو واوا ثم كان قبل الياء والواو حرف مكسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In nominative and genitive, the deleted yāʾ is compensated for by tanwīn, making these forms declinable.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم حذفوا الياء فخف عليهم فصار التنوين عوضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In accusative, inflect a defective form according to whether its sound counterpart is declinable or diptote.
rows.anchor: فإن كان نظيره من غير المعتلة مصروفا صرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extra final yāʾ or wāw preceded by its matching vowel behaves like a radical weak ending.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت من نفس الحرف وهي حرف الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of a radical yāʾ preceded by kasra include قاض, غاز, مغاز, and جوار; forms preceded by ḍamma include أدل and أظب.
rows.anchor: قولك هذا قاض وهذا غاز وهذه مغاز وهؤلاء جوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an added wāw preceded by ḍamma, he gives the plural عرق for عرقوة and a rajaz line containing عرقي.
rows.anchor: وكان الحرف قبلها مضموما فقولك هذه عرق كما ترى إذا أردت جمع عرقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weak ending preceded by fatḥa becomes alif; it is not deleted in pause, and its tanwīn behavior otherwise follows sound nouns.
rows.anchor: أو واو كانت لاما وكان الحرف قبلها مفتوحا فإنها مقصورة تبدل مكانها الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diptote forms عذارى and صحارى take no tanwīn because their final alif completes the mafāʿil pattern.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك عذارى وصحارى فهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final yāʾ or wāw preceded by a consonant with sukūn behaves like a sound ending, as in ظبي and دلو.
rows.anchor: والواو قبلها حرف ساكن وكانت حرف الإعراب فهي بمنزلة غير المعتل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A man named قاض keeps the same inflection as the form had before becoming a proper name.
rows.anchor: وسألت الخليل عن رجل يسمى بقاض فقال هو بمنزلته قبل أن

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A man named جوار has the same nominative and genitive forms as before proper naming; its diptote pattern would resist declension more strongly than قاض.
rows.anchor: حال الجر والرفع بمنزلته قبل أن يكون اسما

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A woman named جوار takes tanwīn because here tanwīn compensates for the deleted yāʾ, as in أذرعات.
rows.anchor: قلت فإن جعلته اسم امرأة قال أصرفها لأن هذا التنوين جعل عوضا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A woman named قاض is declinable in the nominative and genitive; the same pattern applies to a man named أدل.
rows.anchor: وسألته عن قاض اسم امرأة فقال مصروفة في حال الرفع والجر

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A man named أعمى keeps the ordinary diminutive أعيم; أفعل comparatives can take tanwīn in contexts such as خير منك.
rows.anchor: فقال أقول أعيم أصنع به ما صنعت به

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus decides whether a defective proper name is diptote by comparing its sound counterpart as a definite noun, so he says جواري and مررت بجواري.
rows.anchor: يونس فكان ينظر إلى كل شيء من هذا إذا كان معرفة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl rejects Yūnus's rule: if the name followed its sound counterpart, speakers would keep the same nominative and genitive behavior and use the accusative in the indefinite genitive pattern too.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل هذا خطأ لو كان من شأنهم أن

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats tanwīn as a stable substitute for the deleted yāʾ; he rejects a woman's name قاضي retaining yāʾ in the genitive.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل لو قالوا هذا لكانوا خلقاء أن يلزموها الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic necessity can restore weak endings in inflection: the Hudhalī poet has معاري, al-Farazdaq مواليا, and Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt and Jarīr supply further forced forms.
rows.anchor: بهن ملوب كدم العباط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further poetic necessity restores original forms, including يعيليا and سمائيا; the line ألم يأتيك also restores a jussive ending, and al-Kumayt forces ضننوا.
rows.anchor: قد عجبت مني ومن يعيليا

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A man named يرمي or أرمي takes tanwīn, as do the comparable feminine-name forms قاض and أعيم.
rows.anchor: وسألته عن رجل يسمى يرمي أو أرمي فقال أنونه لأنه إذا صار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a man is named غزو, the inflected form is غزي: retaining wāw after ḍamma belongs to verbs, not nouns; the verse about القلنسي supports the noun pattern.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي له أن يكون في قول يونس إلا يغزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proper name should not preserve a form that changes between definite and indefinite use or falls outside Arabic noun patterns; أدلي is offered as evidence.
rows.anchor: كرهوا أن يكون إي وفي في السكوت

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: When the imperative ارمِ becomes a name, restore the weak ending so it can take case, yielding forms such as إرم and إرمي.
rows.anchor: وتقول في رجل سميته بارمه هذا إرم قد جاء وينون في قول الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In naming forms such as عه and يره, restore only a segment belonging to the underlying form, producing وع and إرأ rather than adding an unrelated letter.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس اسم على مثال ع فتصيره بمنزلة الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imperatives قل, خف, بع, and أقم regain their weak radical when made names: قول, خاف, بيع, and أقيم.
rows.anchor: قلت هذا قول قد جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name taken from a jussive clause with لم must preserve the governing construction; where the weak ending is moved, it becomes visible as in يريد and يخاف.
rows.anchor: ولو سميت رجلا لم يرد أو لم يخف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the doubled imperative أعضض yields إعض: the initial hamza is cut and the doubled consonants assimilate, as in the verb pattern أعض.
rows.anchor: إذا حركت اللام من المضاعف أدغمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ألبب remains on its original pattern, like رجاء ابن حيوة and ضيون; Arabic sometimes preserves the source form despite a different usual pattern.
rows.anchor: وإذا سميت رجلا بألبب من قولك قد علمت ذاك بنات ألبب تركته على حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry permits forms excluded from ordinary speech, including declining diptotes and deleting material that speech normally retains.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنه يجوز في الشعر ما لا يجوز في الكلام من صرف ما لا ينصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets sometimes lengthen patterns like مساجد and منابر to مساجيد and منابير; al-Farazdaq's الدنانير illustrates the extension.
rows.anchor: مساجد ومنابر فيقولون مساجيد ومنابير شبهوه بما جمع على غير واحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry can restore the underlying form of weak endings: examples include رادد for راد and ضننوا for ضنوا, witnessed by Qaʿnab's line.
rows.anchor: وقد يبلغون بالمعتل الأصل فيقولون رادد في راد وضننوا في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers geminate words in pause and retain that weight in poetic connected speech, as in سبسبا and كلكلا; several poets illustrate the pattern.
rows.anchor: فهم يجرونه في الوصل على حاله في الوقف نحو سبسبا وكلكلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets also tolerate dispreferred word order when the expression remains complete; the intended prose order is وقل ما يدوم وصال.
rows.anchor: حتى يضعوه في غير موضعه لأنه مستقيم ليس فيه نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In poetry, سواء and the particle كاف may be used like ordinary nouns because سواء means غير and كاف means مثل.
rows.anchor: لأن معنى سواء معنى غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says poets seek a grammatical rationale for every necessity, and that the examples exceed what this brief survey can list.
rows.anchor: وليس شئ يضطرون إليه إلا وهم يحاولون به وجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle with alif-lām, as in الضارب زيدا, functions like the relative هذا الذي ضرب زيدا; the article blocks annexation and acts like tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك هذا الضارب زيدا فصار فى معنى هذا الذى ضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some accepted Arabic usage says الضارب الرجل by analogy with الحسن الوجه, although their meaning and grammatical conditions differ; this noun pattern permits genitive or accusative use.
rows.anchor: وقد قال قوم من العرب ترضى عربيتهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Marrār al-Asadī's التارك البكري بشرا treats بشر as genitive in poetry, by analogy with a form whose tanwīn is blocked.
rows.anchor: أنا ابن التارك البكرى بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When dual or plural participles retain their nūn, their object is accusative, as in الضاربان زيدا and الضاربون الرجل; the Qur'anic المقيمين الصلاة is a parallel.
rows.anchor: أو جمعت فأثبت النون قلت هذان الضاربان زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When nūn is dropped from these forms, the following overt noun is normally genitive; examples include الضاربا زيد and الضاربو عمرو.
rows.anchor: جررت وصار الاسم داخلا فى الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In poetic examples such as الحافظو عورة العشيرة, nūn deletion is not annexation or substitution for nūn but an elision like اللذين, licensed when the phrase grows long.
rows.anchor: للإضافة ولا ليعاقب الاسم النون ولكن حذفوها كما حذفوها من اللذين والذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a connected object pronoun, as in الضاربوك, the pronoun is genitive, not accusative; a bare ضاربو زيدا is unavailable without the relative article.
rows.anchor: هم الضاربوك وهما الضارباك فالوجه فيه الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn and tanwīn must be deleted before a connected pronoun because the pronoun is bound to the host, much like these suffixes at a word's end.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن حذف النون والتنوين لازم مع علامة المضمر غير المنفصل لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports two poetic examples retaining nūn before an attached pronoun, while noting that they were said to be fabricated.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء فى الشعر وزعموا أنه مصنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Independent forms such as أنت and هو can follow attached pronouns in the same case, as in مررت بك أنت and رأيتك أنت.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن هذه الحروف كلها تكون وصفا للمجرور والمرفوع والمنصوب المضمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These pronoun forms are not ordinary adjectives like الطويل; they behave more like نفسه, preserving the grammatical role of the pronoun they accompany.
rows.anchor: ولكنه بمنزلة نفسه إذا قلت مررت به نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pronouns do not describe overt nouns, since that would make an overt noun take a pronominal modifier; this parallels rejecting أجمعون or نفسه after an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الحروف لا تكون وصفا للمظهر كراهية أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun may be replaced by an appositional pronoun: use إياك or إياه for the accusative and أنت or هو for the nominative.
rows.anchor: فأنت وهو وأخواتهما نظائر إياه في النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pronoun can be apposition to an overt noun but not its adjective; apposition is independent, as if the noun were repeated in a new clause.
rows.anchor: رأيت زيدا ثم قلت إياه رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mixed phrase مررت به وبزيد هما is awkward; if intended as apposition, repeat the preposition and say مررت به وبزيد بهما.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه قبيح أن تقول مررت به وبزيد هما كما قبح أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a surah title such as هذه هود, the word سورة is omitted from هذه سورة هود, making the title function like a tribal name.
rows.anchor: تقول هذه هود كما ترى إذا أردت أن تحذف سورة من قولك هذه سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If هود itself is the surah's proper name, it is diptote like a woman named عمرو; surah names are treated like feminine names of women and lands.
rows.anchor: وإن جعلت هودا اسم السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If اقتربت is made a proper name, its initial alif becomes hamzat al-qaṭʿ, like naming a man with إضرب, so it fits noun patterns such as إصبع.
rows.anchor: اقتربت اسما قطعت الألف كما قطعت ألف إضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Titles such as نوح and الرحمن can stand for سورة نوح or سورة الرحمن; if نوح is instead a surah's proper name, it is diptote.
rows.anchor: قولهم هذه الرحمن ولا يكون هذا أبدا إلا وأنت تريد سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حم is indeclinable whether used as a surah name or annexed to it, modeled on foreign names such as هابيل and قابيل; al-Kumayt and al-Ḥammānī give poetic forms.
rows.anchor: وأما حم فلا ينصرف جعلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāsīn and Yāsīn follow the same non-Arabic pattern; some readers treat يس والقرآن and قاف والقرآن as foreign names followed by an implied أذكر.
rows.anchor: لا يجيء في كلامهم على بناء حاميم وياسين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some readers recite يس والقرآن and قاف والقرآن by treating Yāsīn as a foreign name and supplying an implied أذكر.
rows.anchor: فمن قال هذا فكأنه جعله اسما أعجميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صاد can be an Arabic-pattern surah name and then is diptote; alternatively, صاد and ياسين can be indeclinable forms fixed on fatḥa, like كيف, أين, حيث, and أمس.
rows.anchor: صاد فلا تحتاج إلى أن تجعله اسما أعجميا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If طسم is named as one word, change nūn to mīm and join it to Ṭāsīn, like دراب جرد and بعلبك; otherwise quote the letters unchanged.
rows.anchor: لم يكن بد من أن تحرك النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كهيعص and آلمر can only be quoted as letter names: they cannot be compounded by the models discussed or reshaped as إسماعيل because no comparable Arabic pattern exists.
rows.anchor: وأما كهيعص وآلمر فلا يكن إلا حكاية وإن جعلتها بمنزلة طاسين لم يجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نون can be declinable for speakers who decline هند, since نون can be feminine; the unknown meaning of حاميم signals its foreign origin despite Arabic-looking forms such as قابوس.
rows.anchor: وأما نون فيجوز صرفها في قول من صرف هندا
